page: Microsoft Azure E8bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. Running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The configuration features 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, designed for temporary caching, swap space, or high-throughput scratch data, and supports Azure Premium Storage for external managed persistent disks.

Without integrated graphics accelerators, compute resources are strictly centered on general processor operations and large memory allocations. The instance includes 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses, reflecting standard cloud networking topologies where external routing is provisioned separately. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-per-core density and local NVMe storage offer a streamlined profile for workloads requiring low-latency scratch disks alongside significant working memory, avoiding the need to over-provision virtual processor counts just to secure memory capacity.

Because the platform combines dedicated execution threads, an expansive memory footprint, and high-performance local NVMe storage, it targets memory-intensive and I/O-heavy production deployments. Typical workloads include relational database management systems, in-memory caches, enterprise transactional platforms, and data processing pipelines.
